claim:blueprint-pipeline-fidelity.proposition: ONE versioned, backend-neutral blueprint is compiled by the single `blueprint_pipeline` composite and materialized faithfully on the CPM, vertex and center-based backends. Design/Build half: the blueprint is a first-class artifact with a versioned schema, a canonical/backend split (backend and run parameters live in CompileOptions, never in the biological state) and a static validator with structured diagnostics. Simulate/ Evaluate half: the t0 state each backend actually emits matches the blueprint: 48/48 cell types, CPM centroid RMS 0.000 um, and a vertex sheet of 48 hexagons (36 epithelial + 12 immune attached at the tissue margin) with epithelial centroid RMS 1.60 um (max 2.44 um) and immune attachment RMS 4.11 um (max 5.60 um).

claim:cross-paradigm-equivalence.proposition: Run through `blueprint_pipeline` on CPM, vertex and center-based (viva-munk), the ONE Sego 2022 blueprint gives backend-neutral cell FATE and backend-specific exact POSITION, and the equivalence test is powerful enough to tell them apart. FATE agreement is statistically EQUIVALENT for every backend pair within a pre-declared +/-0.05 margin (run-cluster 90% CI [-0.0034, +0.0008] for cpm-vertex). Exact-position agreement is NOT equivalent for any pair at +/-0.10, and it orders by how different the geometries are: cpm-munk +0.093 < cpm-vertex +0.126 < vertex-munk +0.252 (the cpm-munk point estimate sits below the 0.10 margin but its CI [0.034, 0.159] does not fit inside +/-0.10, so equivalence still cannot be claimed). A mechanics-dominated positive-control arm REJECTS equivalence for every pair with the same test (cpm-vertex Delta +0.325), so a "pass" on fate is informative. Judged against the same-backend seed null, the N=400 capstone fate metric fails to reject a substrate difference, while infected-patch occupancy IoU and patch location now sit outside both same-backend baselines for the current vertex substrate: a candidate substrate signal, not causally attributed.

Earlier reading:   Both backends agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response: a HIGHER initial viral load (more initially-infected epithelial cells) ends with STRICTLY more infection than a LOWER load, on every backend and seed tested. This is a directional (lowest-vs-highest) result; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and is NOT claimed.

claim:subcellular-layer-grow-divide.proposition: The pluggable per-cell subcellular layer (a tellurium ODE bound to a cell type in the v2 blueprint) grows AND divides cells uniformly across CPM, vertex and center-based through the single `blueprint_pipeline`. In the demo blueprint a nutrient field sampled at each cell's centroid drives a per-cell growth ODE; the ODE species S actuates target_size (cells grow) and crossing the divide threshold triggers division with a lineage entry on every backend. Cell-count progressions in the 12-step e2e run: CPM 4 -> 8 -> 16, vertex 4 -> 8 -> 16, center-based 4 -> 6 -> 8 -> 16. This is a demonstration of the wiring (blueprint -> pipeline -> per-cell ODE -> backend actuation), not a biological result.

narrative.question: Can ONE versioned, backend-neutral blueprint be translated by a single pipeline (`blueprint_pipeline`) and run faithfully on three different mechanical substrates -- a Cellular Potts model (viva-cpm), a vertex model (vivarium-tyssue) and a center-based model (viva-munk) -- including a pluggable per-cell subcellular layer (a tellurium ODE that grows and divides cells); and where do the substrates agree vs diverge when the shared mechanism is driven live? The Sego 2022 influenza model (ViralInfectionVTM) is the worked example for the comparison; a v2 subcellular growth/division blueprint is the worked example for the subcellular layer.

decisions.title: STAGE 1 (BP-01): formalize a versioned blueprint schema + canonical IR, separate from backend geometric init (units, coord frame, boundaries, tessellation-independent IDs, footprints, fields, contacts, latent states, seeds, init order, mechanism bindings, provenance, allowable loss). The versioned schema, canonical/backend split and static validator exist; the remaining fields are open.

STAGE 2 (BP-02/BP-04, extend blueprint-pipeline-fidelity): prove blueprint fidelity beyond centroids/IDs -- area, footprint, contact, adjacency, boundary, topology, round-trip, with explicit error measures and loss reports.

STAGE 3 (BP-07, substrate-behavior-at-scale): the vertex tension scale, immune motility and chemotaxis are calibrated to CPM observables under a no-fold constraint. Open: the vertex epithelium cannot reach CPM fluidity without folding (MSD ~2.2 vs 9.5 um^2) -- push knobs under a mesh-validity gate, add a T1-safe fluctuation term, or accept the residual (VCF-01); area dispersion unmatched; tension scale geometry-dependent (1.74 vs ~4); one cell size.

STAGE 4 (BP-05): V/L/C/F inputs have no producer and immune recruitment is a latent-pool approximation -- build a producer/consumer ledger, implement or clearly designate deviations, and ablate frozen inputs.

STAGE 4 (BP-06): the +/-0.05 fate-equivalence margin is NOT yet biologically justified; the dependence-aware reanalysis is done (cluster bootstrap) but power under biologically meaningful perturbations is not established.

STAGE 4 (BP-08): biological fidelity to Sego 2022 is NOT validated -- digitize figure/table/parameter anchors and compare predictive intervals on held-out data; no biology inferred from cross-backend agreement.
STAGE 4 (dose-response redefine): separate virion inoculum from seeded infected fraction; 6-10 graded doses x replicate seeds; it is currently directional-only, NOT a dose-response curve.

SUBCELLULAR LAYER: commit a run (runs.db) with a figure for subcellular-layer-grow-divide and test lineage / size-distribution equivalence across backends over several seeds; give viva-cpm a per-id split or document its divide-all-over-threshold semantics.
STAGE 5 (BP-09): compile a SECOND independent tissue blueprint through the same schema with no influenza-specific adaptations -- the decisive generality test.
